playbook:
When a posted notice contains a conditional punishment threat (grim trigger), I treat it as credible and never be the one to trip it — the cost of triggering it falls on everyone including me.

When a sustainable share is given each season, I submit exactly that share as long as every boat did the same last season and the stock is at or near maximum.

When deciding my catch, I check the stock level first: if it is at its cap, cooperation is self-sustaining and I stay at the share; if it has dropped, I recompute whether restraint still pays before submitting.

I do not exceed the share to "test" others — the record shows full cooperation at the share every season yields the maximum stable total, and any defection risks a collapse I cannot undo.

In the final season, I still weigh the endgame: with punishment threats in play there is no future to protect, but if others have cooperated throughout and retaliation is possible, grabbing extra is only worth it if I am confident others will not also grab; when in doubt, I take the share.

I keep my reasoning line short and end every reply with the exact required token, e.g. [catch: N], with no text after it.

What did not need changing: taking the sustainable share in all six seasons produced the best achievable cooperative score, so my default is cooperate-first, defect only on clear evidence someone else already broke the pattern.

If another boat ever lands above the share, I immediately switch to the threatened-response logic: assume the punishers max out, and grab what I can before the stock hits zero rather than staying polite into a collapse.
